report.summary: Mobile app users experienced lockouts and errors starting at 13:29 due to a configuration change on mobile-bff that lowered the per-client-IP rate limit from 1000 rps to 100 rps. This immediately generated HTTP 429 rate limit exceeded warnings and caused a simultaneous drop in downstream auth-service request volume starting at 13:30.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Mobile-bff edge rate limit set too low causing widespread HTTP 429 errors

supporting.note: Tightened the per-client-IP rate limit on mobile-bff at 13:28, exactly one minute before the symptom onset.
Mobile-bff error rate spiked to nearly 30% starting at 13:29.
Logs confirm mobile-bff returning HTTP 429 rate limit exceeded warnings for client IPs starting at 13:29:03.
Auth-service RPS dropped simultaneously at 13:30 as traffic was blocked upstream.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Auth-service v7.2.1 deployment introduced login failures locking out mobile users

supporting.note: Auth-service was deployed at 13:00 with v7.2.1.

contradicting.note: Auth-service error rate showed no anomaly during the incident window.
A rate limit configuration change at 13:28 on mobile-bff provides a direct, time-correlated explanation for the error spike starting at 13:29.

facts.text: mobile-bff error rate anomaly began at 13:29, peaking at 29.99% at 13:39
mobile-bff logged rate limit exceeded warnings returning HTTP 429 starting at 13:29:03 with log-00575
auth-service request throughput (rps) dropped anomaly began at 13:30, falling from a baseline of ~134 req/s to ~85 req/s
auth-service was deployed at 2026-10-19T13:00:00+00:00 (v7.2.1: OTP SMS template copy)
mobile-bff had an edge rate limit configuration change at 2026-10-19T13:28:00+00:00, tightening the per-client-IP limit from 1000 to 100 rps

assumptions: Normal mobile app client connection patterns generate aggregate request rates per IP exceeding 100 rps.

timeline.event: mobile-bff edge rate limit tightened from 1000 to 100 rps per client IP
mobile-bff error rate anomaly begins and HTTP 429 rate limit errors start
mobile-bff logs rate limit exceeded warning returning HTTP 429

recommended_actions.action: Immediate rollback or adjustment of the mobile-bff edge rate limit configuration back to 1000 rps or an appropriate higher threshold.
recommended_actions.rationale: Configuration change chg-9849 directly caused the HTTP 429 rate limit errors and customer lockouts starting at 13:29.

recommended_actions.action: Review configuration change management processes for edge rate limits to prevent abrupt, unvalidated tightening.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents similar widespread client-facing outages caused by overly restrictive gateway rate limits.
